name: Renfield Shake Motor
description:
12V shake motor - 'the signature', Renfield's tremble. BTS7960 / IBT-2 module (sold as HW-039). BCM GPIO: RPWM=12, LPWM=13 (header pins 32 and 33). PROVEN MOVING 2026-09-13 at 30% duty, observed by the operator.

THE TWO THINGS THAT MADE IT WORK, both hardware-only, both of which fail SILENTLY - the wrapper returns success with no motion and nothing in any log says why:
  1. VCC IS A SEPARATE 5V SUPPLY. Unlike the MDD10A this board does not power its logic from the motor rail. VCC -> Pi 5V (header pin 2), GND -> Pi ground (pin 6). Never put 12V on VCC; it destroys the board.
  2. R_EN AND L_EN MUST BE TIED HIGH IN HARDWARE. The software does NOT drive them - setup_bts7960_pins() only writes an enable pin HIGH if renPin/lenPin are configured, and they deliberately are not. Both go to 5V (Pi pin 4 here, same rail as pin 2). Left floating the bridge is disabled and nothing moves.
R_IS and L_IS are current-sense OUTPUTS from the chip, not inputs. Leave them unconnected - jumpering them to VCC can damage it and kills fault detection.

PIN CHOICE: both RPWM and LPWM carry PWM on this board (one at a time, by direction), unlike the MDD10A where DIR was a static level. lgpio.tx_pwm() is SOFTWARE PWM and runs on any GPIO, so nothing today depends on the choice, but 12/13 are the Pi 5's RP1 hardware-PWM pair and would not need rewiring if that ever changes.

12V PATH: B+/B- to the supply, M+/M- to the motor, nothing in line but a slow-blow fuse. No bulk capacitor, no snubber, no series resistor. A fixed resistor can NEVER sit in line with a motor supply - 200 ohm allows 60mA and pins the board near 3.3V; a pre-charge resistor is only valid across a switch that shorts it out.

STILL OUTSTANDING: 10k pull-downs from RPWM and LPWM to ground. With the enables permanently high the bridge is always armed, and a Pi reboot floats both PWM lines - fit them before leaving this unattended.

HISTORY: a Cytron MDD10A was wired here first and destroyed itself with smoke after a couple of minutes powered. Root cause never conclusively established; a reverse-connected bulk electrolytic is the leading candidate. The Pi survived.

Shake is a short burst: scenes run 900-2000ms at 50-80%, maxDuration caps any single energization at 5000ms. A wiper-class motor stalls around 24-40A and cooks until the fuse opens (Groundbreaker, 2026-08-30).

name: Renfield's Eyes
description: Sunplus 1080P Webcam (USB 1bcf:28c4). Proven 2026-08-31 by FRAMES, not status fields: 60 frames/6s from mjpg-streamer on the node, 98 through his own stream endpoint, 296 through Orlok's Fleet Command Center proxy. This entry was recorded in the CHANGELOG but never committed to parts.json - it existed only node-locally, so every config-driven path skipped it. Identify USB devices by idVendor:idProduct, never by per-unit serial. If the device migrates video0<->video1 the /dev/v4l/by-id symlink follows it correctly, which is why the launcher resolves by-id.

name: Renfield Eye Rings
description:
Pair of addressable LED rings used as Renfield's glowing eyes, chained on one data line. Data = BCM GPIO 10 (header pin 19, SPI0 MOSI). 5V and GND from the buck converter, grounds bonded to the Pi.

NOT GPIO 18, AND NOT rpi_ws281x. Every NeoPixel guide says GPIO 18 because rpi_ws281x builds the 800kHz waveform out of the BCM2835/2711 PWM+DMA peripherals. The Pi 5's RP1 removed that register access, so that library cannot work here at all. python_wrappers/neopixel_cli.py generates the same waveform on SPI MOSI instead: each WS2812 bit becomes three SPI bits at 2.4MHz (1 -> 0b110, 0 -> 0b100), both inside the chip's timing tolerance, and MOSI idles low which is the reset condition. Wire order is GRB - the encoder handles it, do not swap it at the call site.

THE 3.3V MARGIN, first suspect if it stays dark while everything reports success: the Pi drives MOSI at 3.3V and a 5V WS2812 wants VIH >= 3.5V. That is BELOW spec. Many rings work anyway and some fail cold. Fix by running the rings on ~4.5V (one silicon diode in their +5V leg drops the threshold to 3.15V) or with a 74AHCT125 level shifter on the data line.

POWER: ~60mA per pixel at full white, so two 16-pixel rings approach 2A. Never off the Pi's 5V header pins - that is the brownout this node already rides close to, since its own 5V comes through the same converter.

STATUS 2026-09-13: driver written and unit-tested (encoding, GRB order, framing) but NEVER RUN AGAINST HARDWARE, and the chip marking on the rings was never confirmed. It is also not yet wired into services/hardwareService - the Node light path still calls light_cli.py, which drives a static level and does nothing to an addressable ring. Prove the rings with the wrapper directly before anyone integrates it.

ledCount is a GUESS of 16. Count the pixels and correct it.
